chunks: And Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad Alawi from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) say: The successor after me is Hasan. But how will it be for you with regard to the successor after the successor? I asked: May I be sacrificed for you, why? He replied: Because you will not see his person, nor is it permissible for you to mention him by his name. I asked: So how are we to mention him? He replied: Say 'The Proof from the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'.

key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a term of respect)

ai.seo_question: How should the Imams be referred to during the period of occultation when their name is not mentioned?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological basis for the 'Minor Occultation' (al-Ghaybah al-Sughra), where Imam al-Askari (a.s.) designates his son Hasan as successor but conceals his identity to prevent premature identification by enemies. The instruction to use the title 'Al-Hujjah' (The Proof) rather than a personal name reflects the Shia scholarly principle of *taqiyyah* (dissimulation) and the unique status of the Imam as the definitive argument of God for humanity during his hidden period.
